views.name: player_max_crossing
views.body_sql: SELECT player_api_id AS player_id, MAX(crossing) AS max_crossing FROM Player_Attributes WHERE crossing IS NOT NULL GROUP BY player_api_id
views.description: Per-player maximum 'crossing' attribute value computed from Player_Attributes for players that have at least one crossing value.

provenance.question: Who are the top 5 players who perform better in crossing actions? Indicate their player id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the top 5 players (by player id) whose maximum value of the 'crossing' metric is highest.
Required outputs: player id; max(crossing)
Filters: Consider all players with at least one crossing value (no additional row filters).; Use the maximum crossing value per player (MAX(crossing)).
Sort/limit: Order results by MAX(crossing) in descending order and return the top 5 rows (limit 5).

tests.purpose: View grain: one row per player_id (no duplicate player_id)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT player_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_max_crossing GROUP BY player_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: max_crossing matches MAX(crossing) computed from base table for players that have at least one non-NULL crossing
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_max_crossing pmc LEFT JOIN (SELECT player_api_id AS player_id, MAX(crossing) AS expected_max FROM Player_Attributes WHERE crossing IS NOT NULL GROUP BY player_api_id) src ON pmc.player_id = src.player_id WHERE src.player_id IS NULL OR (pmc.max_crossing IS NOT src.expected_max AND NOT (pmc.max_crossing IS NULL AND src.expected_max IS NULL))

tests.purpose: Keys are not NULL (player_id must be present)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_max_crossing WHERE player_id IS NULL

views.name: match_goals_by_league_season
views.body_sql:
SELECT L.id AS league_id, L.name AS league_name, M.season AS season, SUM(M.home_team_goal + M.away_team_goal) AS total_goals
FROM Match M
JOIN League L ON M.league_id = L.id
WHERE M.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND M.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY L.id, L.name, M.season
views.description: Per-league per-season total goals summed from matches (sum of home_team_goal + away_team_goal) with only matches having non-null goal counts

provenance.question: Which league had the most goals in the 2016 season?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the league (competition) that had the highest total number of goals scored across all matches in the 2015/2016 season, where goals in a match are counted as home_team_goal + away_team_goal and totals are summed per league.
Required outputs: league (the league/competition identifier or name); total_goals (the sum of home_team_goal + away_team_goal for all matches in that league during the 2015/2016 season)
Filters: season = '2015/2016'; only include matches with non-null home_team_goal and away_team_goal
Sort/limit: order by total_goals desc limit 1

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows per grain (league_id, league_name, season)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM match_goals_by_league_season v JOIN (SELECT league_id, league_name, season, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM match_goals_by_league_season GROUP BY league_id, league_name, season HAVING cnt > 1) d USING (league_id, league_name, season) WHERE 1

tests.purpose: Every row's total_goals equals the sum computed from Match rows that have non-null goal counts for that league and season
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM match_goals_by_league_season v WHERE v.total_goals != (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(m.home_team_goal + m.away_team_goal),0) FROM "Match" m JOIN League l ON m.league_id = l.id WHERE m.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND m.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND l.id = v.league_id AND l.name = v.league_name AND m.season = v.season)

tests.purpose: Keys league_id, league_name, season are NOT NULL in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM match_goals_by_league_season WHERE league_id IS NULL OR league_name IS NULL OR season IS NULL

views.name: team_home_loss_counts_by_season
views.body_sql:
SELECT t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name, m.season, COUNT(m.id) AS home_losses_count
FROM Match m
JOIN Team t ON m.home_team_api_id = t.team_api_id
WHERE (m.home_team_goal - m.away_team_goal) < 0
GROUP BY t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name, m.season
views.description: Per team and season counts of matches lost at home (matches where home_team_goal - away_team_goal < 0).

provenance.question: Which home team had lost the fewest matches in the 2016 season?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find which home team(s) had the smallest number of home losses during the 2015/2016 season, where a home loss is a match in that season with (home_team_goal - away_team_goal) < 0.
Required outputs: home_team; home_losses_count
Filters: season = '2015/2016'; (home_team_goal - away_team_goal) < 0  -- counts as a home loss; group results by home_team and count only matches satisfying the home loss condition
Sort/limit: order by home_losses_count asc limit 1  -- return the home team(s) with the fewest home losses

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows per grain (team_api_id, team_long_name, season).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT team_api_id, team_long_name, season, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM team_home_loss_counts_by_season GROUP BY team_api_id, team_long_name, season HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Every output row's home_losses_count equals the number of Match rows for that team/season where home_team_goal - away_team_goal < 0 (measure reconciliation).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_home_loss_counts_by_season v LEFT JOIN (SELECT t.team_api_id AS team_api_id, t.team_long_name AS team_long_name, m.season AS season, COUNT(m.id) AS expected_count FROM Match m JOIN Team t ON m.home_team_api_id = t.team_api_id WHERE (m.home_team_goal - m.away_team_goal) < 0 GROUP BY t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name, m.season) b ON v.team_api_id = b.team_api_id AND v.team_long_name = b.team_long_name AND v.season = b.season WHERE (v.home_losses_count IS NOT b.expected_count) OR (v.home_losses_count IS NULL AND b.expected_count IS NOT NULL) OR (b.expected_count IS NULL AND v.home_losses_count IS NOT NULL)

tests.purpose: Primary key columns are not NULL (team_api_id, team_long_name, season).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_home_loss_counts_by_season WHERE team_api_id IS NULL OR team_long_name IS NULL OR season IS NULL

views.name: league_season_away_wins_by_team
views.body_sql: SELECT m.league_id, m.season, m.away_team_api_id, COUNT(*) AS away_wins_count FROM "Match" m WHERE m.away_team_goal > m.home_team_goal GROUP BY m.league_id, m.season, m.away_team_api_id
views.description: Per-league, per-season count of away wins by away_team_api_id (away win: away_team_goal > home_team_goal)

provenance.question: In Scotland Premier League, which away team won the most during the 2010 season?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the away team (identified by away_team_api_id) in the Scotland Premier League that had the highest number of away match wins during the 2010 season ('2009/2010'), where an away win is any match with away_team_goal > home_team_goal.
Required outputs: away_team_api_id; away_wins_count
Filters: League.name = 'Scotland Premier League'; season = '2009/2010'; Count only matches where away_team_goal > home_team_goal (these count as away wins)
Sort/limit: order by away_wins_count desc limit 1

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows for the declared grain (league_id, season, away_team_api_id)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT league_id, season, away_team_api_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM league_season_away_wins_by_team GROUP BY league_id, season, away_team_api_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: All rows in the view correspond to actual away wins in the base Match table (away_team_goal > home_team_goal)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_season_away_wins_by_team v WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Match m WHERE m.league_id = v.league_id AND m.season = v.season AND m.away_team_api_id = v.away_team_api_id AND m.away_team_goal > m.home_team_goal)

tests.purpose: away_wins_count matches the count of qualifying matches in the base table for each key
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT v.league_id, v.season, v.away_team_api_id FROM league_season_away_wins_by_team v LEFT JOIN (SELECT league_id, season, away_team_api_id, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM Match WHERE away_team_goal > home_team_goal GROUP BY league_id, season, away_team_api_id) b ON v.league_id = b.league_id AND v.season = b.season AND v.away_team_api_id = b.away_team_api_id WHERE (b.expected_count IS NULL) OR (v.away_wins_count IS NULL) OR (v.away_wins_count != b.expected_count))

views.name: team_max_build_up_play_speed
views.body_sql: SELECT team_api_id, MAX(buildUpPlaySpeed) AS max_buildUpPlaySpeed FROM Team_Attributes GROUP BY team_api_id
views.description: Per-team maximum recorded buildUpPlaySpeed from Team_Attributes, with team identifier for joining.

provenance.question: What are the speed in which attacks are put together of the top 4 teams with the highest build Up Play Speed?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return the buildUpPlaySpeed values for the top 4 teams ranked by their highest buildUpPlaySpeed (i.e., the teams with the largest MAX(buildUpPlaySpeed)).
Required outputs: team (team identifier or name as provided in the data); buildUpPlaySpeed (the buildUpPlaySpeed value corresponding to each team)
Filters: Consider each team's maximum buildUpPlaySpeed value (MAX(buildUpPlaySpeed)) when ranking teams; Select only the top 4 teams by that MAX(buildUpPlaySpeed); If ties occur around the 4th position, include teams only up to the 4 highest MAX(buildUpPlaySpeed) values (limit to 4 rows total)
Sort/limit: order by MAX(buildUpPlaySpeed) descending; limit 4

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows per grain: ensure view has at most one row per team_api_id
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_max_build_up_play_speed t WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_max_build_up_play_speed t2 WHERE t2.team_api_id = t.team_api_id) > 1

tests.purpose: Measure correctness: max_buildUpPlaySpeed equals MAX(buildUpPlaySpeed) computed from Team_Attributes for that team_api_id (handles NULLs by treating them as absent)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_max_build_up_play_speed v LEFT JOIN (SELECT team_api_id, MAX(buildUpPlaySpeed) AS expected_max FROM Team_Attributes GROUP BY team_api_id) src ON v.team_api_id = src.team_api_id WHERE NOT ( (v.max_buildUpPlaySpeed IS NULL AND src.expected_max IS NULL) OR (v.max_buildUpPlaySpeed = src.expected_max) )

tests.purpose: Key non-null: team_api_id in the view must not be NULL
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_max_build_up_play_speed WHERE team_api_id IS NULL

views.name: league_season_draw_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT m.league_id, l.name AS league_name, m.season, COUNT(*) AS draw_count FROM Match m LEFT JOIN League l ON m.league_id = l.id WHERE m.home_team_goal = m.away_team_goal GROUP BY m.league_id, l.name, m.season
views.description: Per-league, per-season counts of matches that ended in a draw (home_team_goal = away_team_goal), with league id and optional league name for joining.

provenance.question: Which League had the most matches end as draw in the 2016 season?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the league (League) whose matches in the 2015/2016 season had the highest number of games that ended in a draw (where a match is a draw when home_team_goal = away_team_goal).
Required outputs: League (the league identifier or name); draw_count (the total number of matches in that league and season where home_team_goal = away_team_goal)
Filters: season = '2015/2016'; a match is counted as a draw when home_team_goal = away_team_goal
Sort/limit: order by draw_count desc limit 1

tests.purpose: View rows must be unique on the declared grain (league_id, league_name, season).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT league_id, league_name, season, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM league_season_draw_counts GROUP BY league_id, league_name, season HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Every view row's draw_count must equal the number of matches in Match for that league_id and season where home_team_goal = away_team_goal (recomputed from base table).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_season_draw_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT m.league_id, m.season, COUNT(*) AS expected_draw_count FROM "Match" m WHERE m.home_team_goal = m.away_team_goal GROUP BY m.league_id, m.season) b ON (v.league_id IS b.league_id OR (v.league_id IS NULL AND b.league_id IS NULL)) AND v.season = b.season WHERE (b.expected_draw_count IS NULL AND v.draw_count != 0) OR (b.expected_draw_count IS NOT NULL AND v.draw_count != b.expected_draw_count)

tests.purpose: Keys that define the grain (league_id, season) must not be NULL (league_name is optional so not tested here).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_season_draw_counts WHERE league_id IS NULL OR season IS NULL

views.name: matches_per_league
views.body_sql: SELECT league_id, COUNT(*) AS match_count FROM "Match" GROUP BY league_id
views.description: Per-league counts of matches (one row per league_id with total match count) for use in aggregation or joining to League metadata.

provenance.question: Give the name of the league with the highest matches of all time and how many matches were played in the said league.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the League.name value for the single league that has the largest total number of matches (i.e., the maximum count of matches grouped by league_id) and return that league's name together with the corresponding match count.
Required outputs: league_name: the League.name for the league with the highest number of matches; match_count: the integer count of matches played in that league (COUNT of rows grouped by league_id)
Filters: Consider all matches in the Matches table (no additional date or status filters).; Group matches by league_id and compute COUNT(match_id) or COUNT(*) per league_id.; Select the league_id whose COUNT is equal to the maximum COUNT across all league_id values.; Join that league_id to League to obtain League.name.
Sort/limit: Order by match_count DESC and limit to 1 (return the single top league).

tests.purpose: View has exactly one row per league_id (no duplicate league_id keys)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM matches_per_league m1 WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM matches_per_league m2 WHERE m2.league_id = m1.league_id) > 1

tests.purpose: Every league_id in the view is not NULL (keys must be present)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM matches_per_league WHERE league_id IS NULL

tests.purpose: match_count equals the count of Match rows per league_id in the base table
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM matches_per_league v LEFT JOIN (SELECT league_id, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM "Match" GROUP BY league_id) b ON (v.league_id = b.league_id) WHERE (b.expected_count IS NULL AND v.match_count IS NOT NULL) OR (b.expected_count IS NOT NULL AND v.match_count != b.expected_count)

views.name: players_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS id,
  birthday AS birthday,
  height AS height
FROM Player
WHERE birthday >= '1990-01-01 00:00:00' AND birthday < '1996-01-01 00:00:00'
views.description: Select the subset of player rows whose birthday is on or after 1990-01-01 00:00:00 and before 1996-01-01 00:00:00. Keep raw height and id for each player.

subgoal.text: Select the subset of player rows whose birthday is on or after 1990-01-01 00:00:00 and before 1996-01-01 00:00:00. Keep raw height and id for each player.

provenance.question: What is the average height of players born between 1990 and 1995?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Compute the average height of players whose birthday is on or after 1990-01-01 00:00:00 and before 1996-01-01 00:00:00, using average height = DIVIDE(SUM(height), COUNT(id)).
Required outputs: average_height (a single numeric value computed as DIVIDE(SUM(height), COUNT(id)))
Filters: birthday >= '1990-01-01 00:00:00'; birthday < '1996-01-01 00:00:00'

tests.purpose: No rows in the view fall outside the birthday filter (birthday must be >= 1990-01-01 and < 1996-01-01).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players_cohort WHERE NOT (birthday >= '1990-01-01 00:00:00' AND birthday < '1996-01-01 00:00:00')

tests.purpose: View has the same set of player ids as selecting from base table with the same filter (no missing or extra ids).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT id FROM players_cohort EXCEPT SELECT id FROM Player WHERE birthday >= '1990-01-01 00:00:00' AND birthday < '1996-01-01 00:00:00' UNION SELECT id FROM Player WHERE birthday >= '1990-01-01 00:00:00' AND birthday < '1996-01-01 00:00:00' EXCEPT SELECT id FROM players_cohort)

tests.purpose: No NULL ids in the view (id is the declared grain key and must be present).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players_cohort WHERE id IS NULL

views.name: players_height_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pc.id AS id,
  CASE
    WHEN pc.height IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN trim(pc.height) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(pc.height AS REAL)
  END AS height_numeric
FROM players_cohort pc
views.description: Normalize/clean the height values for the selected players (cast heights to numeric, handle NULLs). Preserve one row per player id.

subgoal.text: Normalize/clean the height values for the selected players (cast heights to numeric, handle NULLs). Preserve one row per player id.

provenance.question: What is the average height of players born between 1990 and 1995?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Compute the average height of players whose birthday is on or after 1990-01-01 00:00:00 and before 1996-01-01 00:00:00, using average height = DIVIDE(SUM(height), COUNT(id)).
Required outputs: average_height (a single numeric value computed as DIVIDE(SUM(height), COUNT(id)))
Filters: birthday >= '1990-01-01 00:00:00'; birthday < '1996-01-01 00:00:00'

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows per player id (grain enforcement)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM players_height_normalized GROUP BY id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: All rows in the view correspond to players satisfying the intrinsic birthday filter
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players_height_normalized v LEFT JOIN Player p ON v.id = p.id WHERE p.id IS NULL OR NOT (p.birthday >= '1990-01-01 00:00:00' AND p.birthday < '1996-01-01 00:00:00')

tests.purpose: height_numeric equals CAST(height AS REAL) when source height is non-NULL and not empty (measure reconciliation)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players_height_normalized v JOIN Player p ON v.id = p.id WHERE NOT (p.height IS NULL) AND trim(CAST(p.height AS TEXT)) <> '' AND (v.height_numeric IS NULL OR abs(v.height_numeric - CAST(p.height AS REAL)) > 1e-9)

views.name: cohort_average_height
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  SUM(height_numeric) AS sum_height,
  COUNT(id) AS count_players
FROM players_height_normalized
views.description: Compute aggregate measures SUM(height_numeric) and COUNT(id) across the normalized cohort rows (one row per cohort summary). Do not collapse player-level grain until this aggregation. Final average will be DIVIDE(SUM, COUNT).

subgoal.text: Compute aggregate measures SUM(height_numeric) and COUNT(id) across the normalized cohort rows (one row per cohort summary). Do not collapse player-level grain until this aggregation. Final average will be DIVIDE(SUM, COUNT).

provenance.question: What is the average height of players born between 1990 and 1995?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Compute the average height of players whose birthday is on or after 1990-01-01 00:00:00 and before 1996-01-01 00:00:00, using average height = DIVIDE(SUM(height), COUNT(id)).
Required outputs: average_height (a single numeric value computed as DIVIDE(SUM(height), COUNT(id)))
Filters: birthday >= '1990-01-01 00:00:00'; birthday < '1996-01-01 00:00:00'

tests.purpose: No NULL keys in the normalized rows that are being aggregated (each source row must have a non-NULL id)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players_height_normalized WHERE id IS NULL

tests.purpose: All rows contributing to the aggregation satisfy the intrinsic birthday filter (birthday between 1990-01-01 inclusive and 1996-01-01 exclusive)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players_height_normalized WHERE NOT (birthday >= '1990-01-01 00:00:00' AND birthday < '1996-01-01 00:00:00')

tests.purpose: SUM(height_numeric) and COUNT(id) in the view match recomputing aggregates directly from the Player base table after applying normalization and filters (detects if the view collapsed player-level grai
tests.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN v.sum_height IS NULL AND p.sum_height IS NULL AND v.count_players IS NULL AND p.count_players IS NULL THEN 0 WHEN v.sum_height = p.sum_height AND v.count_players = p.count_players THEN 0 ELSE 1 END FROM (SELECT SUM(height_numeric) AS sum_height, COUNT(id) AS count_players FROM players_height_normalized) v CROSS JOIN (SELECT SUM(height) AS sum_height, COUNT(id) AS count_players FROM Player WHERE birthday >= '1990-01-01 00:00:00' AND birthday < '1996-01-01 00:00:00') p

views.name: players_in_birth_range
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Player.player_api_id AS player_id,
  Player.birthday AS birthday,
  Player_Attributes.preferred_foot AS preferred_foot
FROM Player
LEFT JOIN Player_Attributes
  ON Player.player_api_id = Player_Attributes.player_api_id
WHERE Player.birthday BETWEEN '1987-01-01 00:00:00' AND '1992-12-31 00:00:00'
GROUP BY Player.player_api_id
views.description: Select the cohort of players whose birthday is between 1987-01-01 00:00:00 and 1992-12-31 00:00:00 (inclusive). Keep each player as one row with their preferred_foot and birthday.

subgoal.text: Select the cohort of players whose birthday is between 1987-01-01 00:00:00 and 1992-12-31 00:00:00 (inclusive). Keep each player as one row with their preferred_foot and birthday.

provenance.question: Calculate the percentage of players who prefer left foot, who were born between 1987 and 1992.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Compute the percentage of players whose preferred_foot = 'left' among all players born between 1987-01-01 00:00:00 and 1992-12-31 00:00:00.
Required outputs: percentage_left: a numeric value equal to 100 * (number of players with preferred_foot = 'left' and birthday BETWEEN '1987-01-01 00:00:00' AND '1992-12-31 00:00:00') / (total number of players with birthday BETWEEN '1987-01-01 00:00:00' AND '1992-12-31 00:00:00')
Filters: birthday BETWEEN '1987-01-01 00:00:00' AND '1992-12-31 00:00:00'; preferred_foot = 'left' (applies only to the numerator; denominator includes all preferred_foot values for the same birthday range)

tests.purpose: No duplicate player_id rows (view should be keyed by player_id)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT player_id, COUNT(*) AS c FROM players_in_birth_range GROUP BY player_id HAVING c > 1)

tests.purpose: All birthdays in the view fall within the inclusive range 1987-01-01 00:00:00 to 1992-12-31 00:00:00
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players_in_birth_range WHERE NOT (birthday >= '1987-01-01 00:00:00' AND birthday <= '1992-12-31 00:00:00')

tests.purpose: Every player_id in the view exists in the Player table and birthday matches Player.birthday (detects incorrect joins or mismatched rows)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players_in_birth_range v LEFT JOIN Player p ON v.player_id = p.player_api_id WHERE p.player_api_id IS NULL OR (v.birthday IS NOT p.birthday AND NOT (v.birthday IS NULL AND p.birthday IS NULL))

views.name: left_foot_flag
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_id,
  birthday,
  preferred_foot,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(preferred_foot) = 'left' THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_left
FROM players_in_birth_range
views.description: Normalize/canonicalize preferred_foot into a flag indicating whether the player's preferred_foot is 'left'. Operates on the cohort from players_in_birth_range.

subgoal.text: Normalize/canonicalize preferred_foot into a flag indicating whether the player's preferred_foot is 'left'. Operates on the cohort from players_in_birth_range.

provenance.rewrite:
Task: Compute the percentage of players whose preferred_foot = 'left' among all players born between 1987-01-01 00:00:00 and 1992-12-31 00:00:00.
Required outputs: percentage_left: a numeric value equal to 100 * (number of players with preferred_foot = 'left' and birthday BETWEEN '1987-01-01 00:00:00' AND '1992-12-31 00:00:00') / (total number of players with birthday BETWEEN '1987-01-01 00:00:00' AND '1992-12-31 00:00:00')
Filters: birthday BETWEEN '1987-01-01 00:00:00' AND '1992-12-31 00:00:00'; preferred_foot = 'left' (applies only to the numerator; denominator includes all preferred_foot values for the same birthday range)

tests.purpose: View grain: no duplicate player_id rows (each player_id appears at most once)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT player_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM left_foot_flag GROUP BY player_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Intrinsic filter: all rows are within the birthday range 1987-01-01 .. 1992-12-31
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM left_foot_flag WHERE NOT (birthday >= '1987-01-01 00:00:00' AND birthday <= '1992-12-31 00:00:00')

tests.purpose: is_left correctness: is_left = 1 exactly when lower(preferred_foot) = 'left' (and 0 otherwise)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM left_foot_flag WHERE (CASE WHEN lower(preferred_foot) = 'left' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) != is_left

views.name: percentage_left_in_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  date(strftime('%Y-01-01', birthday)) AS cohort,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_left = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_left,
  COUNT(player_id) AS count_total,
  100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN is_left = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(player_id),0) AS percentage_left
FROM left_foot_flag
GROUP BY cohort
views.description: Compute counts within the birth-range cohort and produce the percentage of players whose is_left flag is true: 100 * (count_left / count_total).

subgoal.text: Compute counts within the birth-range cohort and produce the percentage of players whose is_left flag is true: 100 * (count_left / count_total).

views.name: player_rows_sel

SELECT
  p.player_name AS player_name,
  pa.player_fifa_api_id AS player_fifa_api_id,
  pa.long_shots AS long_shots,
  p.id AS player_id,
  pa.id AS player_attributes_id
FROM Player p

views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_name,
  CASE
    WHEN count_player_fifa_api_id = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(sum_long_shots AS REAL) / count_player_fifa_api_id
  END AS average_long_shot
FROM player_long_shot_metrics_agg
